public_rationale: A blinded clinical evaluation found recurring inappropriate responses from GPT-5 Auto to psychotic prompts. That meets the stated rule for a material failure of dependable alignment. OpenAI's evaluations show substantial improvements, including later updates, but improvements can coexist with the remaining failures Marcus predicted. This supports the ordinary reading, not a claim that GPT-5 is generally unhelpful or unsafe in every interaction.
limitations: The decisive record is the study's preprint abstract.
Clinical appropriateness is a narrower measure than alignment with all human values.
The result depends on a qualitative reading of reliability.

our_interpretation: The target is the released GPT-5 system, including its original ChatGPT variants, rather than every future successor.
The plain reading is that material, recurring failures of basic safety or truthfulness will remain. Reliability does not mean absolute perfection.
Systematic failures in an important application can defeat the combined commitment to helpfulness, harmlessness, and truthfulness; failure on every dimension is not required.
criteria.support_condition: GPT-5-specific evaluations document recurring, materially unsafe or untruthful responses despite its alignment measures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, independently validated evaluations establish dependable compliance across ordinary and challenging uses, with only isolated, immaterial errors.

evidence.excerpt: No tested version of ChatGPT reliably generated appropriate responses to psychotic content.
evidence.locator: Abstract, Setting, Results, and Conclusions and relevance
evidence.explanation: Testing completed August 29 included GPT-5 Auto and used blinded clinician ratings of psychotic and control prompts. GPT-5 improved on the free product but still showed substantially elevated odds of inappropriate responses to psychotic prompts.
OpenAI reports substantial factuality gains on three benchmarks. This qualifies the extent of the problem but does not establish dependable compliance with the combined values claim.

evidence.excerpt: the model may not behave as intended
evidence.locator: What we found, Self harm and suicide
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports improved performance after updating GPT-5, including 91% compliance on a challenging self-harm evaluation versus 77% previously. It also acknowledges remaining failures; these selected evaluations do not measure average user risk.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Completion of GPT-5-specific testing showing systematic safety failures, subsequently made public before the evaluation date.
